title: feat: add web component and iframe wrappers

commits.message: feat: add web component and iframe wrappers

fix(wc): address second-round review findings

Correctness:
- Dispatch `nexus-ready` on a microtask. Declarative markup upgrades
  synchronously inside `defineNexusEditor()` and imperative hosts subscribe
  right after `append()`, so the previous synchronous dispatch fired before
  either could attach a listener — the event was unobservable in the flows the
  README documents. Suppressed when the element is detached before the
  microtask runs, so a doomed editor never announces readiness.
- Cancel superseded delayed change notifications for silent `replaceRange`,
  matching the existing `setDocument` fix. Both silent paths now share
  `cancelPendingChangeNotification()`.
- Release bridge change listeners on every terminal failure, not only
  `destroy()` — a TIMEOUT or IFRAME_RELOADED failure retained host closures.
- Preserve an explicit `direction="ltr"` instead of collapsing it to
  `undefined`.

Ergonomics:
- Ship a zero-specificity `:where(nexus-editor){display:block}` rule, injected
  once per document/shadow root, so the element lays out like the React
  wrapper div without boilerplate CSS. Consumer rules still win.
- Observe only `value`, so the element no longer advertises reactivity it does
  not implement.
- Give the iframe runtime's `destroy` override a descriptor matching the
  original data property, so it survives a `{ ...editor }` spread.
- Register `@floatboat/nexus-wc` in `tsconfig.base.json` paths and align
  `files` with react/vue.

Tests (+15, 587 total):
- nexus-ready delivery for post-append and post-define listeners, and
  suppression on immediate disconnect
- focus/blur event forwarding, attribute→config mapping, explicit ltr, NaN
  rejection, theme/locale/onAssetUpload forwarding
- read-only non-reactivity after connect (previously prose-only in the spec)
- createEditor throw rollback and recovery on reconnect
- block display, plus once-per-root injection in a shadow root
- silent replaceRange stale-change regression
- bridge listener release on terminal failure, and the destroy descriptor

Also moves the branch manual checklist from `docs/` into the OpenSpec change
so it is archived with the change instead of accumulating in project docs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

+## Context
+React and Vue bindings (`packages/react`, `packages/vue`) each wrap `createEditor` from `@floatboat/nexus-core` with framework-specific lifecycle glue. Roadmap item 22 asks for framework-agnostic Web Component and iframe wrappers that reuse the same core instance rather than re-implementing editor logic.
+
+## Goals / Non-Goals
+- Goals: expose the same capability surface as `packages/react`'s `<Editor />` as a native custom element, plus a small origin-checked bridge for hosts that render Nexus inside an iframe.
+- Non-Goals: Shadow DOM encapsulation, SSR support, a Vue/React-specific integration layer, proxying the complete `EditorAPI`, shipping or hosting a built-in `frame.html`, and serializing plugins, themes, parsers, upload callbacks, or other function/object configuration across the iframe boundary.
+
+## Decisions
+- **Light DOM, no `attachShadow`.** The element renders a single internal `<div>` child in its own light DOM, exactly like `packages/react`'s wrapper div. Rationale: an unmerged PR (#161) is still fixing a Shadow DOM event-retargeting bug in `plugin-slash` (`event.target` vs `event.composedPath()`); shipping `wc` inside a shadow root today would hit that same unresolved issue for any consumer using the slash plugin. Light DOM sidesteps it entirely and keeps CodeMirror's DOM/coordinate assumptions (popups, `coordsAtPos`) unchanged. Consumers who want encapsulation can wrap `<nexus-editor>` in their own shadow root.
+- **Only `value` is reactive after connection.** `packages/react`'s `useEditor` creates the core editor inside a mount-only effect (`useEffect(..., [])`) — `plugins`, `theme`, `parser`, `tabSize`, etc. are captured once at creation; only the `value` prop is re-synced via a second effect. `wc` mirrors this exactly: `attributeChangedCallback` only reacts to `value`/`initial-value` post-connect; all other attributes/properties are read once in `connectedCallback`. This is capability parity with the existing SDKs, not a new limitation introduced here.
+- **Namespaced, composed custom events (`nexus-*`).** Native elements already dispatch `focus`/`blur`, and `change` is a common native event name (form controls). Using `nexus-focus` / `nexus-blur` / `nexus-change` avoids ambiguity. Events are both bubbling and composed so a consumer-owned shadow root does not hide the public event contract.
+- **Preserve synchronous DOM moves; destroy on true disconnect.** Moving the element between parents fires `disconnectedCallback` and `connectedCallback` synchronously. Teardown is deferred to a microtask and cancelled when the element has already reconnected, preserving uncontrolled edits during reparenting. A genuinely detached element is still destroyed before the next task.
+- **Upgrade pre-definition properties.** Frameworks may assign properties before the lazy custom-element bundle registers. On first connection the element replays own properties through its prototype setters so `value`, plugins, theme, locale, and other public configuration are not shadowed or lost.
+- **Cancel superseded delayed changes in core.** A silent external `setDocument` or `replaceRange` cancels pending parse/composition notifications for the older document. This keeps controlled React, Vue, and Web Component hosts from receiving a stale callback after applying a newer value. Both silent entry points share `cancelPendingChangeNotification()` so the two paths cannot drift.
+- **Dispatch `nexus-ready` on a microtask.** Declarative markup upgrades synchronously inside `defineNexusEditor()`, and imperative hosts subscribe right after `append()` — a synchronous dispatch from `connectedCallback` would fire before either could attach a listener, making the event unobservable in the documented flows. The microtask keeps `.editor` synchronously available while making the event actually reachable. It is suppressed when the element is detached before the microtask runs, so a doomed editor never announces readiness.
+- **Ship a zero-specificity block-display rule.** Custom elements default to `display: inline`, which would wrap CodeMirror's block DOM in an inline box. The element injects `:where(nexus-editor){display:block}` once per root (constructable stylesheet, falling back to a `<style>` element), matching `packages/react`'s wrapper `div` without boilerplate CSS. `:where()` carries zero specificity, so every consumer rule still wins.
+- **Split iframe parent and runtime entry points.** `iframe-parent` owns the `HTMLIFrameElement` and exposes a promise-based controller. `iframe-runtime` runs inside the consumer-hosted frame page, creates the real `EditorAPI`, and supplies all non-serializable editor configuration locally.
+- **Discover globally, communicate privately.** Parent and runtime exchange only versioned `probe`, `runtime-ready`, and `connect` messages through window messaging. Both validate the other window and an exact non-wildcard origin. The connection transfers a `MessagePort`; ready/change events and commands then stay on that dedicated channel.
+- **Detect frame replacement.** Each runtime mount has a unique id. If the same iframe window announces a different runtime id, the parent controller rejects pending work and requires a new controller, preventing commands from silently crossing a reload boundary.
+- **Keep the remote surface deliberately small.** The bridge forwards ready/change, `getDocument`, silent `setDocument`, `focus`, and `destroy`. This covers document embedding without pretending the asynchronous structured-clone boundary is equivalent to the synchronous `EditorAPI`.
+
+## Risks / Trade-offs
+- Non-reactive config (tab size, direction, etc.) may surprise consumers expecting full custom-element reactivity → mitigated by matching documented React/Vue behavior and calling it out explicitly in the README.
+- No Shadow DOM means no built-in style isolation → acceptable per Non-Goals; consumers needing isolation wrap the element themselves.
+- Deferred disconnect cleanup means `.editor` remains non-null until the current microtask completes after permanent removal → acceptable to distinguish true removal from synchronous reparenting.
+- Consumers must host the iframe page and provide exact parent/child origins → explicit configuration avoids unsafe wildcard messaging and assumptions about package asset URLs.
+- Iframe commands are asynchronous and can fail on timeout, reload, or active IME composition → the controller exposes promises and stable error codes; callers retry after composition or create a new controller after reload.
+
+## Migration Plan
+N/A — new package, no existing consumers.
+
+## Open Questions
+- None blocking. Shadow DOM support can be revisited once #161's `composedPath()` fix lands on `main`.

+# Web Component 分支手工测试用例
+
+适用分支：`feat/wc-add-web-component`
+测试目标：验证 `@floatboat/nexus-wc` 新增能力和 review 修复项。
+
+## 1. 测试前准备
+
+```bash
+pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
+pnpm --dir apps/electron-demo exec vite ../../packages/wc/manual --host 127.0.0.1 --port 5173 --strictPort
+```
+
+浏览器打开 `http://127.0.0.1:5173/`。测试台位于 `packages/wc/manual/`，不会进入 npm 发布包。
+
+跨源 iframe 测试需要在第二个终端启动：
+
+```bash
+pnpm --dir apps/electron-demo exec vite ../../packages/wc/manual --host 127.0.0.1 --port 5174 --strictPort
+```
+
+然后打开 `http://127.0.0.1:5173/?frameOrigin=http://127.0.0.1:5174`。
+
+Electron smoke 前先构建 Apple Silicon 安装包：
+
+```bash
+pnpm --filter @floatboat/nexus-electron-demo dist:mac-arm64
+```
+
+产物位于被 Git 忽略的 `apps/electron-demo/release/`，不要加入提交。
+
+> Electron demo 直接使用 Core，不使用 `<nexus-editor>`。WC 生命周期必须在浏览器测试台验证；Electron 只覆盖编辑器整体回归。
+
+## 2. P0：必须通过
+
+### WC-01 基础挂载和事件
+
+前置条件：打开浏览器测试台。
+
+步骤：
+
+1. 在任意编辑器中点击并输入文本。
+2. 打开浏览器控制台，确认没有 uncaught error。
+3. 检查编辑器仍可聚焦、输入、选择文本。
+
+预期：
+
+- 编辑器正常显示并可编辑。
+- 输入后内容立即更新。
+- 页面和控制台没有异常。
+
+### WC-01b nexus-ready 可被注册后的监听器收到
+
+步骤：在浏览器控制台执行：
+
+```js
+const { NexusEditorElement } = await import("/packages/wc/src/index.ts");
+document.body.insertAdjacentHTML("beforeend", '<probe-editor initial-value="# ready"></probe-editor>');
+const el = document.querySelector("probe-editor");
+customElements.define("probe-editor", class extends NexusEditorElement {});
+let fired = 0;
+el.addEventListener("nexus-ready", () => { fired += 1; });   // define 之后才订阅
+await Promise.resolve();
+({ fired, display: getComputedStyle(el).display, doc: el.editor?.getDocument() });
+```
+
+预期：`fired` 为 `1`，`display` 为 `"block"`，`doc` 为 `"# ready"`。
+
+失败证据：`fired` 为 `0`（事件在 `connectedCallback` 内同步派发，宿主来不及订阅），或 `display` 为 `"inline"`。
+
+### WC-01c 默认块级布局
+
+步骤：在控制台执行 `getComputedStyle(document.querySelector("#parent-a nexus-editor")).display`。
+
+预期：返回 `"block"`。测试台的 CSS 只设置 `min-height`，块级来自组件自带的 `:where()` 基础样式。
+
+补充：执行 `document.querySelector("#parent-a nexus-editor").style.display = "flex"`，确认消费方样式能覆盖默认值。
+
+### WC-02 注册前 property 保留
+
+步骤：点击“升级前 property”区域的“检查初始值”。
+
+预期：日志显示：
+
+```text
+PASS WC-02: document="# property before upgrade"
+```
+
+失败证据：文档为空或不是 `# property before upgrade`。
+
+### WC-03 延迟受控同步不回滚
+
+步骤：点击“运行 B → C 竞态”，等待至少 400ms。
+
+预期：日志显示 `PASS WC-03`，并且 `value=C, document=C`。
+
+失败证据：
+
+- `value` 回退成 `B`；或
+- property 与编辑器文档不一致。
+
+### WC-04 同步 reparent 保留未受控内容
+
+步骤：
+
+1. 在“同步 reparent”编辑器中输入一段独特文本，例如 `move-2026`。
+2. 点击“移动并检查”。
+3. 再次点击，移动回原容器。
+
+预期：
+
+- 两次均显示 `PASS WC-04`。
+- 文本、光标和编辑器实例保持可用。
+- 不恢复成 `uncontrolled seed`。
+
+### WC-05 事件穿过 Shadow DOM
+
+步骤：点击“触发 shadow 内变更”。
+
+预期：外层宿主收到事件，日志显示：
+
+```text

+```
+
+## 3. P1：功能完整性
+
+### WC-06 Multi-cursor
+
+步骤：点击“设置两个选区”。
+
+预期：日志显示：
+
+```text
+PASS WC-06: selection ranges=2
+```
+
+### WC-07 永久断开后销毁
+
+在浏览器控制台执行：
+
+```js
+const el = document.querySelector("#multi-mount nexus-editor");
+const api = el.editor;
+el.remove();
+await Promise.resolve();
+({ editorIsNull: el.editor === null, domRemoved: !el.querySelector(".cm-editor"), oldApi: api });
+```
+
+预期：`editorIsNull` 和 `domRemoved` 均为 `true`。
+
+### WC-08 重复注册和外部标签冲突
+
+在控制台执行：
+
+```js
+const { defineNexusEditor } = await import("/packages/wc/src/index.ts");
+defineNexusEditor();
+defineNexusEditor(); // 不抛错
+
+customElements.define("foreign-editor", class extends HTMLElement {});
+try {
+  defineNexusEditor("foreign-editor");
+  console.log("FAIL");
+} catch (error) {
+  console.log("PASS", error.message);
+}
+```
+
+预期：同一 Nexus 标签重复注册无异常；外部构造器占用标签时打印 `PASS`。
+
+### WC-09 初始配置只读取一次
+
+步骤：
+
+1. 在控制台取得任意已连接元素。
+2. 记录当前 `.editor` 引用。
+3. 修改 `readOnly`、`multiCursor` 或 `plugins`。
+4. 尝试继续编辑。
+
+预期：已经创建的 EditorAPI 不被重建，初始配置不会在连接期间动态切换。永久移除并重新添加后，新配置生效。
+
+### WC-10 TypeScript DOM 类型
+
+执行：
+
+```bash
+pnpm --filter @floatboat/nexus-wc exec tsc --noEmit
+```
+
+预期：退出码为 0；`document.querySelector("nexus-editor")`、`event.detail.doc` 无需手写类型断言。

+步骤：直接在 iframe 编辑器内输入文本。

+步骤：

+1. 点击 `setDocument`。

+
+预期：日志依次显示 `PASS IFRAME-03` 和 `PASS IFRAME-04`；程序化 set 不额外产生 IFRAME-02 change。
+
+### IFRAME-05 focus

+步骤：点击 `focus` 后直接输入字符。

+预期：日志显示 `PASS IFRAME-05`，键盘输入进入 iframe 编辑器。

+### IFRAME-06 reload 使旧 controller 失效

+步骤：点击 `reload 检测`，等待 iframe 重载。

+步骤：点击 `destroy`，再点击 iframe 区域或父端 get。

+
+## 5. Electron smoke
+
+### EL-01 安装与启动
+
+步骤：
+
+1. 打开 arm64 DMG。
+2. 将 Nexus Editor 拖入“应用程序”。
+3. 首次启动时，如 macOS 阻止未签名应用，右键应用并选择“打开”。
+
+预期：应用启动，无白屏、崩溃或持续弹窗。
+
+### EL-02 基础编辑回归
+
+步骤：新建或打开 Markdown，依次测试普通输入、撤销/重做、搜索、斜杠菜单、表格和 live preview。
+
+预期：所有操作正常；切换文档后不会晚到旧文档的 change 更新。
+
+## 6. 通过标准与报告模板
+
+合并门槛：全部 P0 和 iframe 用例通过；P1 无功能性失败；Electron 无启动或数据丢失问题。
+
+建议报告格式：
+
+```text

+# Change: Add framework-agnostic Web Component and iframe wrappers (`@floatboat/nexus-wc`)
+
+## Why
+Nexus-Editor ships React and Vue bindings, but teams using Web Components, vanilla JS, other frameworks, or an isolated iframe have no first-class way to embed the engine without hand-rolling `createEditor` lifecycle and cross-window messaging. Roadmap item 22 (`docs/ROADMAP.md`) calls for a `wc` package that shares the core instance model with the existing SDKs.
+
+## What Changes
+- **ADDED** new package `packages/wc` (`@floatboat/nexus-wc`) exporting a `<nexus-editor>` custom element and a `defineNexusEditor(tagName?)` registration helper
+- **ADDED** attribute/property surface mirroring `EditorConfig`: `initial-value` / `value` (controlled, synced via `nexus-change`), `read-only`, `tab-size`, `direction`, `indent-guides`, `live-preview`, `slash-menu-limit`, `parse-delay-ms` as attributes; `plugins`, `parser`, `theme`, `locale`, `onAssetUpload` as JS-only properties (object/function-valued, no attribute equivalent)
+- **ADDED** custom events: `nexus-ready`, `nexus-change`, `nexus-focus`, `nexus-blur`, `nexus-selectionchange`, `nexus-slashmenuchange` — namespaced to avoid colliding with native `change`/`focus`/`blur`
+- **ADDED** `.editor` property exposing the live `EditorAPI` instance (`null` before `connectedCallback` runs)
+- **ADDED** parent and runtime iframe entry points using an origin-checked `MessageChannel` bridge for ready/change, document get/set, focus, and destroy
+- **HARDENED** delayed controlled-value synchronization, custom-element upgrade/reparent lifecycle, and composed event delivery across consumer-owned shadow roots
+
+## Impact
+- Affected specs: new `wc` capability
+- Affected code: new `packages/wc/**` plus the shared delayed-change path in `packages/core`
+- No breaking changes; zero new runtime dependencies (only a workspace dependency on `@floatboat/nexus-core`)

+# WC Spec
+
+## ADDED Requirements
+
+### Requirement: register a `<nexus-editor>` custom element
+`defineNexusEditor(tagName?)` SHALL register the `NexusEditorElement` class as a custom element under the given tag name, defaulting to `nexus-editor`. Calling it more than once with the same tag name SHALL NOT throw.
+
+#### Scenario: default registration
+- **WHEN** `defineNexusEditor()` is called
+- **THEN** `customElements.get("nexus-editor")` SHALL return the `NexusEditorElement` class
+
+#### Scenario: custom tag name
+- **WHEN** `defineNexusEditor("my-editor")` is called
+- **THEN** `customElements.get("my-editor")` SHALL return the `NexusEditorElement` class
+
+#### Scenario: idempotent registration
+- **WHEN** `defineNexusEditor()` is called twice
+- **THEN** the second call SHALL NOT throw
+
+#### Scenario: foreign tag collision
+- **WHEN** the requested tag name is already registered to a different constructor
+- **THEN** `defineNexusEditor(tagName)` SHALL throw instead of silently reporting success
+
+### Requirement: mount a core editor instance on connect
+On `connectedCallback`, the element SHALL create a single light-DOM `<div>` child and construct a `createEditor` instance from `@floatboat/nexus-core` using that div as `container`. On a permanent disconnect, the element SHALL call `editor.destroy()` and remove the internal container after the current microtask. A synchronous disconnect/reconnect caused by DOM reparenting SHALL preserve the live instance.
+
+#### Scenario: editor is available after connecting
+- **WHEN** a `<nexus-editor>` element is appended to the document
+- **THEN** `element.editor` SHALL be a non-null `EditorAPI` synchronously after `connectedCallback` returns
+
+#### Scenario: element lays out as a block by default
+- **WHEN** a `<nexus-editor>` element connects with no consumer stylesheet
+- **THEN** its computed `display` SHALL be `block`
+- **AND** any consumer rule targeting the tag SHALL override that default
+
+#### Scenario: editor is destroyed on disconnect
+- **WHEN** a connected `<nexus-editor>` element is removed from the document
+- **THEN** after the current microtask the underlying `EditorAPI.destroy()` SHALL have been called and `element.editor` SHALL be `null`
+
+#### Scenario: synchronous reparent preserves uncontrolled edits
+- **WHEN** an uncontrolled element is moved synchronously between connected parents
+- **THEN** its live `EditorAPI` and current document SHALL be preserved
+
+### Requirement: controlled and uncontrolled document value
+The `initial-value` attribute SHALL seed the document once at connect time (uncontrolled mode). The `value` attribute/property SHALL put the element in controlled mode: external changes SHALL be applied via `setDocument(value, { silent: true })`, and user edits SHALL be reported via the `nexus-change` event without re-applying the value that produced them.
+
+#### Scenario: uncontrolled initial value
+- **WHEN** `<nexus-editor initial-value="# Hello"></nexus-editor>` connects
+- **THEN** `element.editor.getDocument()` SHALL return `"# Hello"`
+
+#### Scenario: controlled value updates the document silently
+- **WHEN** `element.value = "next"` is set after the element is connected
+- **THEN** `element.editor.getDocument()` SHALL return `"next"`
+- **AND** no `nexus-change` event SHALL fire for that programmatic update
+
+#### Scenario: skip redundant sync when value matches last emitted change
+- **WHEN** `element.value` is set to the same string most recently emitted via `nexus-change`
+- **THEN** the element SHALL NOT call `setDocument` again for that value
+
+#### Scenario: newer controlled value supersedes delayed change
+- **WHEN** an older user change is waiting for `parse-delay-ms` and the host applies a newer controlled value
+- **THEN** the older delayed change SHALL NOT be emitted after the newer value is applied
+
+### Requirement: forward editor lifecycle and interaction events
+The element SHALL dispatch `CustomEvent`s named `nexus-ready`, `nexus-change`, `nexus-focus`, `nexus-blur`, `nexus-selectionchange`, and `nexus-slashmenuchange`, each `bubbles: true`, `composed: true`, and carrying the corresponding core payload in `event.detail`.
+
+#### Scenario: nexus-ready carries the editor instance
+- **WHEN** the element connects and finishes creating the editor
+- **THEN** a `nexus-ready` event SHALL fire with `event.detail.editor` equal to `element.editor`
+
+#### Scenario: nexus-ready reaches a listener attached after connection
+- **WHEN** a host attaches a `nexus-ready` listener immediately after appending the element, or immediately after `defineNexusEditor()` upgrades declarative markup
+- **THEN** that listener SHALL still receive the event, which is dispatched on a microtask rather than synchronously
+
+#### Scenario: nexus-ready is suppressed for an element detached before dispatch
+- **WHEN** the element is removed from the document before the pending `nexus-ready` microtask runs
+- **THEN** no `nexus-ready` event SHALL fire for the editor that is about to be destroyed
+
+#### Scenario: nexus-change carries doc and ast
+- **WHEN** the user edits the document
+- **THEN** a `nexus-change` event SHALL fire with `event.detail.doc` (string) and `event.detail.ast` (mdast Root)
+
+### Requirement: initial-only configuration parity with React/Vue bindings
+Attributes and properties other than `value`/`initial-value` (`read-only`, `tab-size`, `direction`, `indent-guides`, `live-preview`, `multi-cursor`, `slash-menu-limit`, `parse-delay-ms`, `plugins`, `parser`, `theme`, `locale`, `onAssetUpload`) SHALL be read once when the editor is created and SHALL NOT trigger a live reconfiguration when changed after connection, matching `packages/react`'s `useEditor` mount-only creation effect. `value` SHALL be the only entry in `observedAttributes`, so the element does not advertise reactivity it does not implement. Properties assigned before custom-element registration SHALL be replayed through the upgraded element's setters before configuration is read.
+
+#### Scenario: changing read-only after connect does not affect the live editor
+- **WHEN** `element.readOnly` is set to `true` after the element has connected
+- **THEN** the already-created `EditorAPI` instance's editability SHALL remain unchanged until the element is reconnected
+
+#### Scenario: pre-upgrade property is preserved
+- **WHEN** a host assigns `value` or another public property before `defineNexusEditor()` upgrades the element
+- **THEN** the upgraded element SHALL initialize from that assigned property
+
+#### Scenario: multi-cursor configuration is forwarded
+- **WHEN** `multi-cursor` is present before connection
+- **THEN** the created editor SHALL allow multiple selection ranges
+
+### Requirement: publish TypeScript DOM integration
+The package declaration surface SHALL register `nexus-editor` in `HTMLElementTagNameMap` and type all public `nexus-*` events.
+
+#### Scenario: query the default element in TypeScript
+- **WHEN** a TypeScript consumer calls `document.querySelector("nexus-editor")`
+- **THEN** the result SHALL be typed as `NexusEditorElement | null`
+
+### Requirement: connect a parent page to an iframe runtime
+The `@floatboat/nexus-wc/iframe-parent` entry point SHALL export `connectNexusIframe(iframe, options)`. It SHALL require an exact non-wildcard `targetOrigin`, discover the runtime only from the supplied iframe window and origin, and transfer a dedicated `MessagePort` after a versioned handshake.
+
+#### Scenario: origin-checked connection becomes ready
+- **WHEN** the supplied iframe announces a compatible runtime from `targetOrigin`
+- **THEN** `controller.ready` SHALL resolve after the dedicated port reports ready
+
+#### Scenario: wildcard origin is rejected
+- **WHEN** `targetOrigin` is `"*"`, opaque, or contains a path
+- **THEN** `connectNexusIframe` SHALL throw before sending a message
+
+#### Scenario: incompatible or unrelated messages are ignored
+- **WHEN** a message has a different source window, origin, protocol name, or version
+- **THEN** it SHALL NOT connect or control the iframe runtime
+
+### Requirement: proxy the minimal iframe editor surface
+`NexusIframeController` SHALL expose asynchronous `getDocument`, `setDocument`, and `focus` methods, an `onChange` subscription, and synchronous `destroy`. Programmatic `setDocument` SHALL be silent inside the runtime so controlled hosts do not receive their own value as a user change.
+
+#### Scenario: document round trip
+- **WHEN** the parent sets a document and then gets it
+- **THEN** the returned document SHALL equal the value applied in the iframe
+- **AND** the set operation SHALL NOT emit a change event
+
+#### Scenario: user edit crosses the iframe boundary
+- **WHEN** the editor inside the iframe reports a document change
+- **THEN** every active parent `onChange` listener SHALL receive the new document string
+
+#### Scenario: request times out
+- **WHEN** a ready runtime does not answer a command within `timeoutMs`
+- **THEN** that command promise SHALL reject with a stable `TIMEOUT` bridge error
+
+#### Scenario: document replacement during IME composition
+- **WHEN** the parent requests `setDocument` while the iframe editor is composing text
+- **THEN** the request SHALL reject with `COMPOSING`
+- **AND** the runtime SHALL NOT acknowledge or queue the replacement
+
+### Requirement: mount an iframe runtime around the core editor
+The `@floatboat/nexus-wc/iframe-runtime` entry point SHALL export `mountNexusIframeRuntime(options)`. It SHALL require execution inside an iframe and an exact `allowedParentOrigin`, create an `EditorAPI` from the locally supplied `editorConfig`, and accept a compatible connection only from `window.parent` at that origin.
+
+#### Scenario: runtime configuration stays local
+- **WHEN** the runtime mounts with plugins, parsers, themes, or callbacks in `editorConfig`
+- **THEN** those values SHALL be passed directly to `createEditor` and SHALL NOT be serialized through window messaging
+
+#### Scenario: runtime is destroyed remotely
+- **WHEN** the parent controller sends destroy
+- **THEN** the runtime SHALL remove its listeners, close its port, and destroy the core editor
+
+### Requirement: invalidate a bridge across iframe reload
+Every runtime mount SHALL have a unique runtime id. A controller connected to one runtime SHALL fail when the same iframe announces a different runtime id, and the host SHALL create a new controller for the replacement runtime.
+
+#### Scenario: iframe reloads after connection
+- **WHEN** a connected iframe loads and announces a different runtime id
+- **THEN** pending and subsequent controller operations SHALL reject with `IFRAME_RELOADED`
+
+#### Scenario: replacement page does not mount a runtime
+- **WHEN** a connected iframe fires load but no compatible runtime answers within `timeoutMs`
+- **THEN** the controller SHALL become terminal and subsequent operations SHALL reject with `IFRAME_RELOADED`

+# @floatboat/nexus-wc
+
+Framework-agnostic bindings for [Nexus-Editor](https://github.com/floatboatai/Nexus-Editor): a `<nexus-editor>` custom element for direct embedding and a typed bridge for consumer-hosted iframe pages.
+
+Use this package when embedding Nexus-Editor from vanilla JS, Web Components, or a framework without a dedicated binding (`@floatboat/nexus-react` and `@floatboat/nexus-vue` exist for React and Vue).
+
+## Install
+
+```bash
+pnpm add @floatboat/nexus-wc @floatboat/nexus-core @floatboat/nexus-preset-gfm
+```
+
+## Quick start
+
+```ts
+import { defineNexusEditor } from "@floatboat/nexus-wc";
+
+defineNexusEditor(); // registers <nexus-editor>, no-op if already registered
+```
+
+```html
+<nexus-editor initial-value="# Hello"></nexus-editor>
+```
+
+```ts
+const el = document.querySelector("nexus-editor");
+
+el.addEventListener("nexus-ready", (event) => {
+  console.log(event.detail.editor.getDocument());
+});
+
+el.addEventListener("nexus-change", (event) => {
+  console.log(event.detail.doc);
+});
+```
+
+The element mounts a real `EditorAPI` instance (from `@floatboat/nexus-core`) into an inner `div` on connect. A permanent disconnect destroys it after the current microtask; a synchronous move between DOM parents preserves the live instance and uncontrolled edits.
+
+### Reading the instance
+
+`.editor` is available **synchronously** once the element has connected, so the direct read is usually the simplest option:
+
+```ts
+document.body.append(el);
+el.editor?.getDocument(); // ready
+```
+
+`nexus-ready` is dispatched on a microtask after the editor is created, so a listener attached immediately after `append()` (or after `defineNexusEditor()` upgrades declarative markup) still receives it. Only listeners attached later — in a `setTimeout`, or after an `await` — can miss the event; use `.editor` in that case.
+
+### Layout
+
+The element sets `display: block` through a zero-specificity `:where()` rule, so it lays out like `@floatboat/nexus-react`'s wrapper div without any boilerplate CSS. Any consumer rule wins over it. The element has no intrinsic height, so give it one where your layout needs it:
+
+```css
+nexus-editor {
+  min-height: 300px;
+}
+```
+
+## Controlled usage
+
+Set the `value` property (or attribute) to make the parent own the markdown string. External updates are applied with a silent `setDocument` so the editor does not echo another `nexus-change` for the same content.
+
+```ts
+const el = document.querySelector("nexus-editor");
+el.value = "# Hello";
+
+el.addEventListener("nexus-change", (event) => {
+  state.doc = event.detail.doc;
+});
+
+// Later, an external update:
+el.value = state.doc;
+```
+
+Use `initial-value` instead when the editor should own edits after mount (uncontrolled).
+
+| Mode | Attribute/property | Owner updates |
+|------|---------------------|----------------|
+| Controlled | `value` | Set `value`; keep it in sync via `nexus-change` |
+| Uncontrolled | `initial-value` | Optional; editor owns edits until you call `EditorAPI` |
+
+## Iframe bridge
+
+Use the iframe entry points when the editor must run in a separate browsing context. The package supplies both ends of the bridge; the consuming application supplies and hosts the frame page.
+
+Parent page:
+
+```ts
+import { connectNexusIframe } from "@floatboat/nexus-wc/iframe-parent";
+
+const iframe = document.querySelector<HTMLIFrameElement>("#editor-frame")!;
+const controller = connectNexusIframe(iframe, {
+  targetOrigin: "https://editor.example.com",
+  timeoutMs: 5_000,
+});
+
+await controller.ready;
+await controller.setDocument("# Hello from the parent");
+console.log(await controller.getDocument());
+
+const unsubscribe = controller.onChange((doc) => console.log(doc));
+await controller.focus();
+
+// Later:
+unsubscribe();
+controller.destroy();
+```
+
+Consumer-hosted iframe page:
+
+```ts
+import { mountNexusIframeRuntime } from "@floatboat/nexus-wc/iframe-runtime";
+import { createGfmPreset } from "@floatboat/nexus-preset-gfm";
+
+const editor = mountNexusIframeRuntime({
+  container: document.querySelector("#editor")!,
+  allowedParentOrigin: "https://app.example.com",
+  editorConfig: {
+    initialValue: "# Waiting for the parent",
+    plugins: [createGfmPreset()],
+    livePreview: true,
+  },
+});
+```
+
+Both origins are required and must be exact origins such as `https://app.example.com`: wildcard (`*`), opaque, and path-bearing values are rejected. Discovery validates `event.source`, origin, protocol version, and a per-runtime id before transferring a dedicated `MessagePort`. If the iframe reloads, create a new controller. Plugins, parsers, themes, locales, and callbacks remain in the iframe's local `editorConfig`; they are never serialized across the boundary.
+
+The bridge intentionally exposes only asynchronous ready/change, `getDocument`, silent `setDocument`, `focus`, and `destroy`. Code that needs the complete synchronous `EditorAPI` should run inside the iframe or use `<nexus-editor>` directly.
+
+Bridge failures reject with `NexusIframeBridgeError`. Stable codes include `TIMEOUT`, `IFRAME_RELOADED`, `DESTROYED`, `MESSAGE_ERROR`, `REMOTE_ERROR`, and `COMPOSING`. A `COMPOSING` response means the iframe is in an active IME composition; no replacement was queued, so retry `setDocument` after composition ends.
+
+## Attributes and properties
+
+Everything except `value` is read once in `connectedCallback` — matching the mount-only creation effect used by `@floatboat/nexus-react`'s `useEditor`. Reconnecting the element (disconnect + reconnect) re-reads all of them.
+
+| Name | Kind | Type | Notes |
+|------|------|------|-------|
+| `value` | attribute + property | `string` | Reactive; controlled document |
+| `initial-value` | attribute | `string` | Uncontrolled seed document |
+| `read-only` | attribute + property (`readOnly`) | boolean | |
+| `tab-size` | attribute | `number` | |
+| `direction` | attribute | `"ltr" \| "rtl"` | |
+| `indent-guides` | attribute | boolean | |
+| `live-preview` | attribute | boolean | Use the `livePreview` property for a full `LivePreviewConfig` |
+| `multi-cursor` | attribute + property (`multiCursor`) | boolean | Enables multiple selection ranges at connect time |
+| `slash-menu-limit` | attribute | `number` | |
+| `parse-delay-ms` | attribute | `number` | |
+| `plugins` | property | `NexusPlugin[]` | JS-only, no attribute equivalent |
+| `parser` | property | `ParserLike` | JS-only |
+| `theme` | property | `NexusTheme` | JS-only |
+| `locale` | property | `Partial<NexusLocale>` | JS-only |
+| `livePreview` | property | `boolean \| LivePreviewConfig` | Overrides the `live-preview` attribute |
+| `onAssetUpload` | property | `(file: File) => Promise<string \| null>` | JS-only |
+| `editor` | property (readonly) | `EditorAPI \| null` | `null` until `connectedCallback` runs |
+
+## Events
+
+All events are namespaced with a `nexus-` prefix to avoid colliding with native `change`/`focus`/`blur`. They bubble and are composed, so delegated listeners also work outside a consumer-owned shadow root.
+
+| Event | Detail |
+|-------|--------|
+| `nexus-ready` | `{ editor: EditorAPI }` |
+| `nexus-change` | `{ doc: string, ast: Root }` |
+| `nexus-focus` | — |
+| `nexus-blur` | — |
+| `nexus-selectionchange` | selection snapshot (see `EditorEventMap["selectionChange"]`) |
+| `nexus-slashmenuchange` | `SlashMenuState` |
+
+## Custom tag names
+
+`defineNexusEditor` accepts an optional tag name for apps that need to avoid a collision:
+
+```ts
+defineNexusEditor("my-nexus-editor");
+```
+
+Calling `defineNexusEditor` again for the same Nexus constructor is a no-op. If another component already owns the requested tag name, the helper throws so the collision cannot be mistaken for a successful registration.
+
+## Manual verification
+
+From the repository root, start the parent test bench and an optional cross-origin frame server in separate terminals:
+
+```bash
+pnpm --dir apps/electron-demo exec vite ../../packages/wc/manual --host 127.0.0.1 --port 5173 --strictPort
+pnpm --dir apps/electron-demo exec vite ../../packages/wc/manual --host 127.0.0.1 --port 5174 --strictPort
+```
+
+Open `http://127.0.0.1:5173/?frameOrigin=http://127.0.0.1:5174` for the cross-origin case.
+
+The complete Chinese checklist is in [`openspec/changes/add-wc-wrapper/manual-test.zh.md`](../../openspec/changes/add-wc-wrapper/manual-test.zh.md).
